outcome: Contribution of each Robson group to the overall Cesarean section rate
cohort: The study included all 9110 births (vaginal deliveries and Cesarean sections) occurring in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at a tertiary care center over a one-year period from October 2021 to September 2022.
finding: Out of 9110 total deliveries, 5036 (55.27%) were Cesarean Sections, with the highest contribution to the overall CS rate coming from Robson Group X (22.85%), followed by Group V (20.63%).
mod_finding: The mean Cesarean Section rate was 55.06%, with Group X (women with a single cephalic pregnancy at term with a previous Cesarean section, in spontaneous or induced labor, or before labor) and Group V (women with a single cephalic pregnancy at term with a previous Cesarean section undergoing planned CS) being the highest contributors to the overall CS rate.
